name: Abigail Moejoh
bio: Abigail Moejoh is a 500-level Pharmacy student at the University of Lagos, a health-tech innovator, and a leader passionate about growth, service, and meaningful impact. Having served in the leadership of the National Fellowship of Christian Pharmacy Students (NFCPS) for two years, she has led student development and innovation initiatives, including the PharmaTether community and Pharmathon. Passionate about building at the intersection of health and technology, she has won several hackathons, earning prizes and grants worth over ₦4 million. As President of PANS UNILAG, she is committed to purposeful leadership, collaboration, and initiatives that equip pharmacy students with the skills, knowledge, and opportunities they need to thrive both during their studies and beyond graduation.

name: Adeyinka Olanrewaju
bio: Adeyinka Olanrewaju is a 400-level Pharmacy student at the University of Lagos with experience in student representation, fundraising, and committee leadership. She has served as a Senator, Fundraising Team Lead, and committee member for initiatives including Health Week, Pharmathon, Senate Day, and PANS Trivia. As Vice President, she supports the President, oversees Health Week, and contributes to student welfare initiatives. Her interests include event planning, volunteering, and building effective structures for student-led projects.

name: Oluwole Opeyemi
bio: Oluwole Opeyemi is a 500-level Pharmacy student at the University of Lagos and serves as the Secretary General of PANS UNILAG. She coordinates the Secretariat, manages official correspondence and documentation, records meetings, and communicates executive decisions. Through these responsibilities, she contributes to effective administration and the smooth operation of the association.

name: Temilade Wealth Elizabeth
bio: Temilade Wealth Elizabeth is a 300-level Pharmacy student at the University of Lagos with a strong interest in student development, leadership, and capacity building. She previously served as a Senator representing the 200-level constituency during the 2025/2026 tenure and participated in various subcommittees within the association. As Assistant Secretary General, she supports administrative operations, manages correspondence, assists with the oversight of association properties, and promotes student participation and development.

name: Adeyeri Kehinde Precious
bio:
Adeyeri Kehinde Precious is a 400-level Pharmacy student at the University of Lagos, currently serving as the Treasurer of the Pharmaceutical Association of Nigerian Students (PANS), University of Lagos Chapter.

Prior to assuming this position, she served in various leadership capacities, including as the ADMAP Coordinator for the 2025/2026 administrative session. She has also contributed to the planning and execution of several events, serving as an Assistant Team Lead for ADMAP Rally and as part of the Welfare team during Health Week 2025/2026.

Beyond her formal leadership roles, Kehinde has volunteered in various capacities across health advocacy, sports, academics, welfare and fashion. These experiences reflect her commitment to service, teamwork, and contributing meaningfully to different aspects of student life.

As Treasurer of PANS UNILAG, she is committed to carrying out her responsibilities with accountability, transparency, and dedication to the association.

name: Ogunyemi Oluwatofunmi Quayyum
bio:
Ogunyemi Oluwatofunmi Quayyum is a 400-level Pharmacy student at the University of Lagos and a First Class student who has received numerous scholarships and academic support awards. He is interested in data analytics and how it can be applied to pharmacy to improve research, support clinical decisions, and enhance patient care.

He currently serves as the Financial Secretary of the Pharmaceutical Association of Nigeria Students (PANS), University of Lagos, for the 2026–2027 administration. His role involves managing financial records, preparing budgets, monitoring expenditure, and promoting accountability in the association’s finances. He is committed to ensuring that funds are properly managed and used to support the association’s activities and projects.

Before his current position, he served as a Senator representing the 200-level constituency in the PANS UNILAG Senate. He also served as Assistant Director of Studies of the Pharmaceutical Association of Muslim Students of Nigeria (PMSSN), where he contributed to academic support and student development.

Outside academics and student leadership, he works as an AI content creator, producing AI-generated videos, faceless YouTube documentaries, and promotional content for different brands. He enjoys exploring new ways to use artificial intelligence in content creation and digital storytelling. He is also interested in financial markets, particularly forex trading, market analysis, and investing.

He is passionate about learning, leadership, and personal development. He hopes to build a career that combines his background in pharmacy with his interest in data analytics while continuing to grow in content creation and financial market analysis.

name: Adedipe Maliq Olamide
bio: Adedipe Maliq Olamide is a 300-level Doctor of Pharmacy student at the University of Lagos with experience in publicity, editorial work, and event hosting. He previously served as Assistant Publicity Team Lead for PANS UNILAG SDG during the 2025/2026 session, co-hosted Pharmathon 3.0, and participated in the COMPSSA Editorial Board. Passionate about writing, digital media, healthcare, research, and entrepreneurship, he is also developing skills in videography, graphic design, video editing, and educational content creation. As Public Relations Officer, he leads communication and publicity efforts, strengthens engagement between PANS UNILAG and its members, and works towards building a more visible and connected association through Project AUREA 26/27.

name: Ajose Shamsudeen
bio: Ajose Shamsudeen is a 300-level Pharmacy student at the University of Lagos with interests in leadership, sports, volunteering, mentorship, and creative writing. He co-hosted Fresher’s week panel session during the 2025/2026 session, and has participated actively as a member under several subcommittees. Being an active student of his class, he’s always committed time to carrying his fellow coursemates along. He is also an active member of the Pharmaceutical Muslims student society of Nigeria (PMSSN). He is passionate about personal and academic growth and strives to balance his studies with leadership and service. He also enjoys writing reflective pieces on life and love and is committed to developing his creative writing skills. As Assistant Public Relations Officer, he supports the association’s publicity and communication efforts, serving as a link between PANSites and the Executive Council while promoting accessibility, engagement, and unity within PANS UNILAG.

name: Oyawoye Anuoluwapo
bio: Oyawoye Anuoluwapo is a 500-level Pharmacy student with a passion for creativity, writing, healthcare innovation, and community impact. A natural storyteller and creative thinker, she enjoys transforming ideas into engaging narratives and visual experiences. Her experience includes leadership in health technology and volunteering in community health initiatives. She is also interested in research, data analytics, and digital innovation, with a commitment to creating meaningful solutions that improve lives.

name: Arigbabowo Abdulraheem Anuoluwapo
bio: Arigbabowo Abdulraheem Anuoluwapo is a 400-level Pharmacy student at the University of Lagos with interests in event planning, teamwork, student engagement, and leadership. He has served on the PANS Social Committee and volunteered in student welfare, sports, publicity, logistics, and event coordination. He is also a member of the Ingenium Basketball Team and participates in the PANS Public Health Team, PANS Research Team, and ADMAP. As Social Secretary, he coordinates social activities that foster connection, unity, and an engaging student experience for pharmacy students.

name: Adekoya Oyinkansola Isabella
bio: Adekoya Oyinkansola Isabella is a 300-level Pharmacy student at the University of Lagos who is passionate about leadership, self-development, and service. She has served in various leadership capacities, including as a member of the association’s legislative arm, where she represented her constituency, and as a class representative. She also actively participates in volunteering activities within PANS. Through her role as Assistant Social Secretary, she contributes to student engagement and association activities while seeking opportunities to grow personally and professionally.

name: Akintoye Mahmud Korede
bio: Akintoye Mahmud Korede is a 400-level Pharmacy student at the University of Lagos with a strong interest in sports, teamwork, and leadership. He previously participated as a PANS football player and served on the PANS Sports Committee during the 2025/2026 session. He has competed in interfaculty and Pharmalympics events, earning medals, including a gold medal in the Provost Cup football competition. As Sports Secretary, he coordinates sporting activities and competitions while promoting sportsmanship, teamwork, and unity among pharmacy students.

name: Farayola Fawaz Damola
bio: Farayola Fawaz Damola is a 400-level Pharmacy student at the University of Lagos with interests in sports, teamwork, student engagement, and leadership. He previously served as a Sports Representative for ULSP and was a member of the PANS Sports Committee during the 2025/2026 session. He has also participated in interfaculty and pharmacy sporting competitions, earning medals in football and athletics-related events. As Assistant Sports Secretary, he supports the coordination of sporting activities and promotes sportsmanship, student participation, teamwork, and unity among pharmacy students.

name: Ojo Temidayo Ajoke
bio: Ojo Temidayo Ajoke is a 500-level Pharmacy student passionate about leadership, service, personal development, and community impact. She previously served as Senate Leader during the 2025/2026 academic session and as Chairperson of the PANS Health Week Committee. As Welfare Secretary, she is committed to student welfare, effective representation, and initiatives that improve the student experience. Beyond academics and leadership, she is an aspiring entrepreneur interested in healthcare innovation, pharmaceutical research, and business development.
